The second additionally supplies an unsupported final number.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J01707","case1_error":"Leading answer marker says 15, but the derivation and concluding answer correctly give 21.","case2_error":"Leading answer marker says 1000, but the derivation and concluding answer correctly give 1250.","reason":"Both contain only answer-marker conflicts with otherwise correct mathematics, requiring an uncertain judgment.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J01708","case1_error":"Treats the 12-apple excess as the entire green-apple count, obtaining 28 instead of 44 total apples.","case2_error":"Replaces the correctly calculated $5700 goal with funds raised plus miscellaneous expenses, producing an erroneous remaining balance.","reason":"The first confuses a comparative difference with a category total; the second incorrectly redefines an already established funding goal.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01709","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 18 months plus 6 years as 8.5 years instead of 7.5 years.","case2_error":"Subtracts the dog’s eyes from an already net consumption figure, then divides eyes among people without converting eyes to fish.","reason":"The first numerically evaluates a correct expression incorrectly; the second uses incorrect quantity relationships and omits the eyes-to-fish conversion.","judgment":"different"}]}
